issues.title: Undefined viscosity symbol in the trace estimate
issues.failure_explanation: Estimate I1 begins with 2 mu_f times the interface product. Applying Young's inequality preserves that same factor in both resulting terms, so the jump coefficient must be mu_f/delta_1. The old symbol mu is not defined as a model parameter and is inconsistent with the calculation immediately above it.
issues.overall_effect: Read literally, the auxiliary trace estimate has an undefined coefficient and cannot be invoked in the subsequent coercivity and invertibility chain.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In estimate I1, replace the undefined coefficient μ/δ_1 by μ_f/δ_1 and use that corrected estimate in every dependent invocation. No hypothesis, construction, or proof argument otherwise needs to change.
issues.why_classification: The two preceding lines carry the factor 2μ_f through Young's inequality, and μ_f is the only relevant defined viscosity. Thus the old source uniquely forces this transcriptional correction, with no mathematical inference to repair.

issues.title: Wrong-sign interface lower bound in coupled coercivity
issues.failure_explanation: The definition of b_Gamma is a negative product of the free-fluid normal stress and the normal-velocity jump, so it is sign-indefinite. More decisively, set v_f=0 and w_s=0 and choose an admissible v_r with nonzero normal trace. Then b_Gamma(v_f,v_r,w_s;v_f,0)=0, while the old claimed lower bound contains the strictly positive jump term epsilon^{-1} sum h_E^{-1}||v_r·n_P||^2. Thus the displayed lower bound cannot hold. The correct estimate has two negative Young terms that must be absorbed by viscosity and a sufficiently large penalty.
issues.overall_effect: Uniform ellipticity of A is not proved under the old hypotheses, so the later kernel, semidiscrete well-posedness, fixed-point, and old fully discrete nonsingularity arguments that invoke this ellipticity are unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the asserted positive lower bound for the interface term by the trace/Young estimate b_Γ ≥ -δ C_tr^2 μ_f‖ε(v_f)‖^2 - (μ_f/δ)Σ_E h_E^{-1}‖J‖_E^2, where J is the normal-velocity jump, including the applicable Nitsche symmetry factor. Estimate a_f^S+b_Γ+c_Γ as a whole, choose δ so the viscous remainder is positive, and require the penalty coefficient to absorb the negative jump term. Recalibrate the generic coercivity and small-data constants and carry the same penalty condition through the dependent invertibility and semidiscrete fixed-point results.
issues.why_classification: The old proof uses a genuinely false sign, so this is not a typo. Nevertheless, the correction is the standard local Nitsche coercivity absorption already mirrored in the later energy estimates. A sufficiently large penalty is part of the intended regime, and the repair preserves the operator, conclusions, rates, and method without a new lemma or proof architecture.

issues.title: Insufficient temporal load assumptions for semidiscrete solution regularity
issues.failure_explanation: The old theorem claims componentwise W^(1,infinity)/L^infinity temporal solution regularity although the data declarations only specify pointwise spatial membership. Take f_S=0, theta=0, and f_P(t)=t^(-1/2)g with nonzero discrete load projection. The resulting load vector in Mx'+Nx=L(t) is unbounded, contradicting boundedness of the claimed solution and derivative components. Temporal boundedness of the complete load is necessary for this argument, but it has not been shown sufficient for the stated regularity of this differential-algebraic system.
issues.overall_effect: The linearized theorem and its dependent fixed-point theorem lack a justified temporal data-to-solution regularity contract. Bounded loads remove the displayed counterexample but do not by themselves close the differential-algebraic regularity argument. This root does not establish numerical failure or invalidity of the fully discrete scheme.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify sufficient temporal regularity for every load in the complete semidiscrete system, including the constraint source r_S. Identify which algebraic constraints require time derivatives of the data, and supply a constraint-aware finite-dimensional argument giving the claimed regularity of each solution component. Carry the same assumptions into the dependent fixed-point theorem thm:added-1 and use the appropriate time-uniform norm in its small-data condition. Compatible initial data remain the separate I004 prerequisite. The exact sufficient assumptions and complete replacement proof remain unverified. The authors add L^infinity assumptions on f_S, f_P, and theta and compatible initial data in v2, but do not explicitly qualify r_S and retain the generic regular-pencil invocation and erroneous no-zero-rows argument. This is partial repair evidence, not proof that bounded loads suffice; the latter reasoning is separately represented by I004.
issues.why_classification: The formerly proposed L^infinity amendment does not establish a complete routine repair. Identifying constraint-dependent data requirements and proving the componentwise temporal regularity requires additional contained mathematical work. Moderate is the accepted bounded assessment: a contained differential-algebraic regularity repair is credible, while global reconstruction or major mathematical loss has not been established. Its exact sufficient assumptions and full proof are still unverified, and the author revision alone does not settle them.

issues.title: Missing DAE compatibility hypothesis for initial data

failure_location.quote: The matrix \(E\) has no zero rows, which implies that the system has no algebraic constraints.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: if the matrix pencil \(s\,\mathbf{M} + \mathbf{N}\) is nonsingular for some \(s\neq 0\) and the initial data are consistent, then the system \eqref{mixed-primal} admits a solution.

issues.failure_explanation: The old theorem applies to the inherited given initial values, and the old proof itself states that the invoked DAE theorem requires consistent initial data. It then asserts consistency merely because the derivative matrix has no zero rows. That implication is false: the displayed M is singular, including an all-zero derivative column for the free-fluid pressure, so descriptor constraints cannot be dismissed from row nonzeroness. The earlier phrase 'suitable approximations' does not define or establish DAE consistency.
issues.overall_effect: Existence in E+H and well-definedness of the subsequent fixed-point map are not established for arbitrary inherited initial data.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require the prescribed discrete initial vector to be consistent with the semidiscrete DAE in the sense of the cited DAE theorem, and impose the same compatibility premise in the theorem defining the fixed-point map. Define the stated suitable finite element approximations to lie in that consistency set, or use a constraint-preserving projection. Delete the assertion that absence of zero rows eliminates algebraic constraints and invoke the DAE theorem using the explicit compatibility hypothesis.
issues.why_classification: The row argument is invalid and a real premise is missing, so the defect is substantive rather than typographical. DAE consistency is, however, a standard local admissibility condition for a classical solution; inconsistent initial vectors cannot satisfy the asserted evolution. Adding this qualification preserves the well-posedness result for the intended admissible initial-data regime without changing the method or requiring new proof architecture.

issues.title: Invalid scaled-pencil invertibility inference

failure_location.quote: This resulting matrix has the same structure as $\mathbf{M} + \mathbf{N}$, which is shown to be nonsingular in the proof of Lemma~\ref{invertibilty}. Therefore, the scaled matrix is nonsingular

issues.failure_explanation: Invertibility of the pencil at s=1 does not imply invertibility at s=1/tau. Even in the scalar case M=1 and N=-2, M+N=-1 is invertible, whereas for tau=1/2 the scaled matrix tau^{-1}M+N is zero. Sharing a saddle-point sparsity pattern supplies no missing spectral argument, and the old proof gives no estimate valid at the actual time-step value.
issues.overall_effect: The old fully discrete theorem does not establish unique solvability at every time step; the later a priori estimates can at most be read conditionally on a solution until a time-step operator argument is supplied.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the structural-analogy inference by a kernel argument for L_τ=τ^{-1}M+N. For a homogeneous one-step difference, test with the same variables while scaling the solid-displacement test component by τ^{-1}. Extract the resulting coercive one-step estimate from the subsequent stability calculation, using the stated convection smallness and a sufficiently large Nitsche penalty. It forces the velocity, displacement, porous-pressure, and solid-velocity components to vanish; the discrete inf-sup condition then gives the remaining pressure. Hence ker L_τ={0}, and because L_τ is a square finite-dimensional matrix it is invertible for every τ>0.
issues.why_classification: Invertibility at s=1 does not justify invertibility at s=1/τ, so this is not a typo. A complete short bypass is nevertheless already supported by the old source's one-step energy and inf-sup calculations: their homogeneous specialization proves injectivity, after which finite dimensionality gives existence. This local replacement preserves the all-time-step solvability guarantee and needs no new spectral lemma or global reconstruction.

issues.title: Missing square in the fully discrete temporal error term
issues.failure_explanation: The theorem estimates squared errors. The backward-Euler residual enters the energy argument quadratically after Young's inequality, and the Taylor/Cauchy estimate has the form tau sum ||r_n(u_f)||^2 <= C tau^2||partial_tt u_f||_{L^2}^2. Thus the proof supports a squared temporal norm, not the displayed first power; there is no uniform conversion from x^2 to x for unrestricted x.
issues.overall_effect: One temporal regularity contribution in the main fully discrete error bound is malformed, although the tau^2 convergence order and the rest of the estimate are unchanged by the correction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the missing exponent 2 on the temporal regularity norm, so the contribution is τ^2‖∂_{tt}u_f^S‖_{L^2(I;L^2(Ω_P))}^2. No other part of the estimate or its proof needs alteration.
issues.why_classification: The theorem estimates squared errors, all neighboring energy contributions are quadratic, and the backward-Euler residual estimate followed by Young's inequality uniquely produces the squared norm. The proof and the τ^2 convergence order already use that reading, so the missing exponent is purely transcriptional.
